question:
A 22-year-old woman with stage 4 chronic kidney disease (CKD) due to focal segmental
glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) presents for a routine follow-up. She was diagnosed with FSGS three years
ago and currently has an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of 18 mL/min/1.73 m² (reference
range, ≥60). She has been intermittently treated with glucocorticoids since her diagnosis but
experiences flares when she discontinues therapy. As a result of glucocorticoid use, she has
developed hyperglycemia, with fasting blood glucose levels typically below 130 mg/dL but occasional
postprandial spikes exceeding 200 mg/dL. Despite counseling, she prefers not to initiate insulin therapy
and inquires about a safe noninsulin medication option. Which of the following antidiabetic medications

is most appropriate for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Metformin (B) Empagliflozin (C) Semaglutide
(D) Exenatide (E) Sitagliptin (F) Glimepiride (G) Canagliflozin (H) Pioglitazone (I) Dapagliflozin (J)
Linagliptin
 A. Semaglutide
B. Linagliptin
C. Canagliflozin
D. Sitagliptin
E. Pioglitazone
F. Empagliflozin
G. Glimepiride
H. Dapagliflozin
I. Exenatide
J. Metformin
